verified.story_title: USCG Cutter Waesche debuts V-BAT surveillance drone during 113-day Bering Sea patrol
verified.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Waesche (WMSL 751) returned from a 113-day, roughly 18,685-nautical-mile Bering Sea patrol that included the initial operational integration of the V-BAT vertical-takeoff unmanned aircraft system, providing persistent airborne ISR from the cutter's deck, plus the first-ever fueling-at-sea exercise with the new polar icebreaker USCGC Storis in Dutch Harbor.

First-ever fueling-at-sea with new icebreaker USCGC Storis in Dutch Harbor
113-day patrol, ~18,685 nautical miles

verified.story_title: GCI Aleutian subsea fiber break cuts six communities (May 27)
verified.summary: A GCI subsea fiber cable severed between Larsen Bay and Chignik Bay on May 27, cutting internet and wireless service to Akutan, Chignik Bay, False Pass, King Cove, Perryville, and Unalaska, with a repair vessel transit estimated at 7 to 14 days. GCI partially restored mobile voice and texting via backup satellite. It was the second Aleutian subsea break in roughly six months (prior December outage near Mount Ballyhoo).
confirmed_facts: Six communities affected (Akutan, Chignik Bay, False Pass, King Cove, Perryville, Unalaska)
Break between Larsen Bay and Chignik Bay
7-14 day repair vessel timeline (GCI's Megan Webb, per Broadband Breakfast)
Backup satellite partial restoration
GCI 151,200 cable broadband subscribers, down 3% YoY
Prior December 2025 Aleutian break
softening_required: STRIP the $310M Quintillion acquisition figure — not confirmed on any fetched page.
verified.industry_consequence: Telecom / edge connectivity. Six remote communities on capped satellite backup for up to two weeks; repeated single-point subsea failures raise redundancy and subscriber-attrition pressure on GCI and an opening for LEO satellite competitors.

verified.story_title: Alaska Legislature passes first unemployment benefit increase since 2009
verified.summary: On the final day of the 2026 session, Alaska lawmakers voted to raise the maximum weekly unemployment benefit from $370 to $470 and to triple the dependent allowance from $24 to $72 per week, the first increase since 2009, with sponsors citing retention of Alaska's seasonal construction and oil-and-gas workforce. The measure awaits Gov. Dunleavy's signature.
confirmed_facts: Max weekly benefit $370 -> $470 (ADN, Alaska Public, Governing)
Dependent allowance $24 -> $72/week
First increase since 2009
Awaits Gov. Dunleavy signature
Rep. Zack Fields cited the most seasonal workforce in the country (construction, oil and gas)

verified.industry_consequence: Workforce retention. A retention lever for the skilled-trades and technical labor pool that any AI-infrastructure or autonomy buildout would draw against; effect contingent on the governor's signature.
